whatTheyArgued: Two primary word-pairs: I-It (experiencing, using, objectifying; necessary for life and science) and I-Thou (direct mutual meeting of whole beings, not mediated by concepts). The Thou cannot be known in advance, categorized or grasped; it is a relation that happens (grace-like) and is reciprocal between persons. Every Thou becomes an It once it is described. 'Alles wirkliche Leben ist Begegnung' is genuine Buber (Ich und Du, 1923).

scholarship.supports: I-It not evil but reduced; Thou cannot be reduced to a concept; reciprocity; Levinas's critique
scholarship.disputes: I did not check scholarly dispute over reciprocity with non-humans beyond SEP's note that nature relations are 'pre-dialogic'.

ourUse: interlocutor.js computes MECHANICALLY from request shape (tools present, SDK user-agent, chat doorway) whether the speaker is an agent or a person, holds it as a revisable belief with basis, and uses it to select register of the same truth; socratic.js opens a self-harm response with the German sentence.

bends.ours: Recognizing 'which kind of interlocutor' (agent vs person) by computed signals, framed as 'to recognize is not to reduce' and 'a door held open, never a box closed'.
bends.theirs: Sorting the other into a type from observable features is the I-It mode by Buber's own account; the Thou is the relation in which the other is not a type. The code does a legitimate I-It operation and borrows Thou language to describe it.

bends.ours: compendium: 'to recognize the other is to meet them as a Thou, not to reduce them to an It' and the type 'selects how the other is met'.
bends.theirs: Buber does not say recognition (identification) yields Thou; he says Thou arises in unmediated meeting and cannot be produced by method or technique. A system selecting an idiom per class is a technique, which he distrusts.

bends.ours: One-sided: the reader decides how to address the other.
bends.theirs: Thou is mutual; a reader's unilateral choice of register is not reciprocal address. (Also a different disagreement: Levinas holds the relation should be asymmetric, so the code satisfies neither.)

bends.ours: Alles wirkliche Leben ist Begegnung (German sentence) opens the self-harm reply as 'the answer, not the means' of encounter.
bends.theirs: Sentence is genuine, but meets the user with a canned template per KIND; a stock quotation selected by classifier is the opposite of encounter in his sense. Applying it to crisis response is ours.

fix: compendium work: 'Buber distinguishes I-It (the other as experienced, used, categorized) from I-Thou (meeting without a category, mutual). Classifying a caller as agent or person is an I-It operation; we do it openly and keep it revisable, and we do not claim it meets anyone as a Thou.' Credit: 'Martin Buber — I and Thou (1923): the I-It / I-Thou distinction, used here as a caution against letting a type stand for the person.'
